examples.ko: 어릴 때 위인전기를 읽고 과학자가 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I read a biography of a great person and wanted to become a scientist.
I borrowed a biography of King Sejong from the library.
Even elementary school students can read this biography easily.

examples.ko: 위인전기에는 어려운 시기를 이겨 낸 이야기가 많아요.
examples.en: Biographies of great people have many stories of overcoming hard times.
I gave the child a biography as a gift.
I find novels more fun than biographies.

explain: 줄여서 '위인전'이라고도 해요. 주로 어린이 책이나 독서 이야기에서 나오고, 한 사람의 삶을 따라가며 교훈을 주는 책이라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is also shortened to '위인전'. It mostly comes up in talk about children's books and reading, and it suggests a book that follows one person's life and offers a lesson.

examples.en: If an agent comes in your place, a letter of attorney is a must.
The bank told me to submit a letter of attorney.

examples.ko: 위임장에 도장을 찍고 신분증 사본도 붙였어요.
examples.en: I stamped the letter of attorney and attached a copy of my ID too.

examples.ko: 위임장은 개인이 작성하는 사문서라서 도장이나 서명이 필요해요.
examples.en: A letter of attorney is a private document written by an individual, so it needs a seal or signature.

examples.ko: 위임장 없이는 서류를 받을 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't pick up the documents without a letter of attorney.
I got a letter of attorney form from the community center.

explain: 본인이 직접 못 할 때 다른 사람에게 일을 맡긴다는 내용을 적는 서류예요. 보통 '위임장을 쓰다/내다/제출하다'로 말하고, 은행·주민센터·회사에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the document you write when you cannot do something yourself and let someone else do it for you. People usually say '위임장을 쓰다/내다/제출하다', and it often comes up at banks, community centers and companies.

examples.en: Experts judged that painting to be a forgery.
There was a big controversy over a forgery at the art museum.

examples.ko: 위작을 진짜처럼 속여 판 사람이 잡혔어요.
examples.en: The person who sold a forgery as if it were real was caught.
This piece of pottery is quite likely a fake.
It is really hard to tell a forgery from the genuine article.
A forgery of a famous painter's work showed up on the market.

explain: '가짜'보다 딱딱한 말이고, 그림·글씨·도자기 같은 예술품에 주로 써요. 반대말은 '진품'이고, 일상에서 물건이 가짜라고 할 때는 그냥 '가짜'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '가짜' (fake) and is mainly used for artworks such as paintings, calligraphy and pottery. The opposite is '진품' (genuine article), and for everyday fake goods people just say '가짜'.

examples.en: Those in power must listen to the voice of the people.
The responsibility of those who lead a country is heavy.

examples.ko: 위정자가 약속을 지키지 않으면 신뢰를 잃어요.
examples.en: If policymakers don't keep their promises, they lose trust.

examples.ko: 옛날 위정자들도 백성의 삶을 살폈다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that rulers in the old days also looked after the lives of their people.
This article sharply criticizes those in power.
What a statesman needs most is honesty.

explain: '정치인'은 일상에서 두루 쓰는 말이고, '위정자'는 정치를 맡은 사람들을 무겁게 말하는 글말이에요. 뉴스 사설, 역사 글, 비판하는 글에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: '정치인' (politician) is the everyday word, while '위정자' is a weighty, written-style word for people who run the government. You will see it in editorials, history writing and critical essays.

examples.ko: 서류를 고친 사람이 위조죄로 재판을 받았어요.
examples.en: The person who altered the documents was tried for forgery.

examples.ko: 위조죄는 법에 따라 처벌받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Forgery can be punished under the law.
He forged a passport, so the forgery charge was applied.

examples.ko: 위조죄 혐의를 받던 사람이 무죄를 주장했어요.
examples.en: The person suspected of forgery claimed to be innocent.
The lawyer said that forgery was not established.

examples.ko: 도장을 몰래 만들어도 위조죄에 해당할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Secretly making a seal can also count as forgery.

explain: 앞에 '문서 위조죄', '화폐 위조죄'처럼 무엇을 위조했는지 붙여서 말하는 경우가 많아요. 일상에서는 '위조'라고 하고, '위조죄'는 뉴스나 재판 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: It is often used with the thing forged in front, as in '문서 위조죄' or '화폐 위조죄'. In daily talk people say '위조', and '위조죄' appears in news and court stories.

examples.en: Grandfather's condition is critical, so the family gathered.
I heard the patient's condition is very critical.

examples.ko: 위중한 상황이지만 의료진이 최선을 다하고 있어요.
examples.en: It is a critical situation, but the medical staff are doing their best.
The person who was in the accident is in critical condition.

examples.ko: 병원에서 상태가 위중하니 빨리 오라고 했어요.
examples.en: The hospital said his condition is critical and told me to come quickly.
My father is critically ill, so I took leave from work.

explain: 주로 병세나 환자의 상태가 생명이 걱정될 만큼 나쁠 때 써요. '위독하다'와 비슷하고, 윗사람 이야기를 할 때는 '위중하세요/위중하셔서'처럼 높여요.
explain_en: It is mainly used when an illness or a patient's condition is bad enough that life is at risk. It is close to '위독하다', and for someone senior you raise it as '위중하세요' or '위중하셔서'.

examples.en: I became a committee member and received a letter of appointment.
The ceremony for presenting letters of appointment is held in the morning.
The term of office is written on the letter of appointment.
The letter of appointment was handed to the new advisory member.
Please keep your letter of appointment safe.
I received a letter of appointment together with a business card.

explain: 위원, 자문위원, 홍보대사처럼 어떤 역할을 맡아 달라고 할 때 주는 증서예요. 보통 '위촉장을 받다/수여하다/전달하다'로 쓰고, 공식 행사나 공공기관 소식에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the certificate given when someone is asked to take on a role such as committee member, adviser or ambassador. It is normally used as '위촉장을 받다/수여하다/전달하다' and often appears in official events and public-institution news.

examples.ko: 아이가 난간 위에 서 있어서 위태위태해요.
examples.en: The child is standing on the railing, so it looks very precarious.
There is a rumor that the company's situation is shaky.
Watching him walk so unsteadily made me nervous.

examples.ko: 짐을 너무 높이 쌓아서 위태위태해 보여요.
examples.en: The load is piled so high that it looks like it could fall.
His health is in a precarious state.
The score gap was small, so it was nerve-racking.

explain: '위태하다'를 반복해서 곧 무너지거나 떨어질 것처럼 아슬아슬한 느낌을 더 생생하게 말해요. '아슬아슬하다'와 비슷하지만, 건강·회사·관계처럼 눈에 안 보이는 상황에도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It repeats '위태하다' to give a vivid sense of something about to collapse or fall. It is close to '아슬아슬하다', but it is also often used for things you cannot see, such as health, a company or a relationship.

examples.en: My stomach pain was bad from the morning, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 위통 때문에 점심을 거의 못 먹었어요.
examples.en: Because of the stomach pain, I could hardly eat lunch.

examples.ko: 위통을 줄이려면 천천히 먹는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: To reduce stomach pain, it is good to eat slowly.
After I took medicine, the stomach pain eased.

examples.ko: 위통과 구토가 함께 나타나면 진료를 받으세요.
examples.en: If stomach pain and vomiting appear together, see a doctor.

examples.ko: 위통의 원인을 찾기 위해 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: I had an exam to find the cause of the stomach pain.

explain: 일상에서는 '속이 아파요', '배가 아파요', '속이 쓰려요'처럼 말하는 경우가 많고, '위통'은 병원이나 약 설명에서 잘 나와요. 배 전체가 아픈 '복통'과 달리 위 쪽 통증을 가리켜요.
explain_en: In daily talk people often say '속이 아파요', '배가 아파요' or '속이 쓰려요', while '위통' shows up in hospital and medicine explanations. Unlike '복통', which is pain in the belly generally, it points to pain around the stomach.

examples.ko: 위패들 사이에 놓인 아버지 사진을 올려다봤어요.
examples.en: I looked up at my father's photo placed among the spirit tablets.
We enshrined my late grandmother's spirit tablet at the temple.
There are ancestral tablets in the family shrine.

examples.ko: 위패에는 돌아가신 분의 이름이 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The name of the deceased is written on the spirit tablet.
I lit incense and prayed in front of the spirit tablet.
I carefully wiped even the spirit tablets.

explain: 돌아가신 분의 이름을 글씨로 적어 모시는 나무판이라서, 사진인 '영정'과 구별돼요. 제사나 절, 사당 이야기에서 나오고 보통 '위패를 모시다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is a wooden tablet with the name of a deceased person written on it, so it differs from '영정', which is a portrait photo. It comes up when talking about ancestral rites, temples and shrines, and people usually say '위패를 모시다'.

examples.en: The soldiers marched majestically.
The pine tree standing on the mountaintop looks imposing.
The lion walked toward us with a commanding presence.
Even the once-majestic castle has now collapsed.
My father in a suit looks especially dignified today.
That general looked truly majestic.

explain: 사람, 동물, 건물이 크고 힘 있어 보여서 감탄할 만할 때 쓰는 칭찬이에요. '위풍당당하게 걷다/행진하다/서 있다'처럼 모습이나 걸음과 자주 같이 나와요.
explain_en: It is a compliment for a person, animal or building that looks big and powerful enough to impress you. It often goes with appearance or movement, as in '위풍당당하게 걷다/행진하다/서 있다'.

examples.ko: 밤에 불빛 없이 산길을 걷는 건 위험천만해요.
examples.en: Walking a mountain path at night without a light is extremely dangerous.
Speeding on a wet road is an extremely dangerous thing to do.
I saw a child crossing the road in a very dangerous way.
That bridge was so old that crossing it was extremely dangerous.

examples.ko: 소방관은 불 속에 들어가는 일이 위험천만하다고 말했어요.
examples.en: The firefighter said that going into a fire is extremely dangerous.
Please don't play any pranks that look extremely dangerous.

explain: '위험하다'보다 훨씬 강해서 큰 사고가 날 수 있다는 경고의 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스나 안전 안내, 사고 이야기에서 자주 보이고, 가벼운 일에는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '위험하다' and carries the feel of a warning that a serious accident could happen. You often see it in news, safety notices and accident stories, and it is not used for small matters.

en: colder part of an ondol room, away from the heat source

examples.en: The warm end of the floor is cozy, but the far end is a bit cold.
The water I left at the cold end of the room froze solid.
I moved my seat to the cold end of the room.

examples.ko: 윗목에서 자면 밤에 추울 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you sleep at the cold end, you may feel cold at night.
The blanket at the cold end of the room was chilly.

examples.ko: 방이 넓어서 윗목까지 온기가 잘 안 와요.
examples.en: The room is big, so the warmth doesn't reach the far end well.

explain: 온돌방에서 불을 때는 쪽에서 먼, 상대적으로 차가운 쪽을 말해요. 반대말은 '아랫목'이고, 옛날 집이나 한옥 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In a Korean heated-floor room, it is the side far from the heat source, which stays relatively cold. The opposite is '아랫목', and it often comes up when talking about old houses and hanok.

examples.ko: 윗물이 맑아야 아랫물이 맑다는 속담이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a proverb that the lower stream is clear only if the upper stream is clear.

examples.ko: 윗물에서 쓰레기를 버리면 아래 마을이 피해를 봐요.
examples.en: If people dump trash upstream, the villages below suffer.
The factory polluted the upstream water.

examples.ko: 윗물 쪽 마을에서는 물을 아껴 쓰자고 했어요.
examples.en: The villages on the upstream side said we should save water.
The upstream water is clear, but the downstream water is cloudy.
Change has to start from the top of the company.

explain: 강이나 개울의 위쪽 물이라는 뜻이지만, 윗사람이나 조직의 위쪽을 비유할 때도 자주 써요. 반대말은 '아랫물'이고, 속담 때문에 '윗물이 맑아야…'라는 말로 많이 알려져 있어요.

phrases.example: 윗물이 맑아야 아랫물이 맑다고, 사장님이 먼저 모범을 보여야 해요.
phrases.en: Those at the top must set a good example for those below.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이 바르게 행동해야 아랫사람도 따라서 바르게 행동한다는 속담이에요. 리더의 책임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that people below will behave well only if those above do. It is used when talking about a leader's responsibility.

explain_en: It means the water in the upper part of a river or stream, but it is also often used figuratively for people at the top of an organization. The opposite is '아랫물', and it is best known through the proverb '윗물이 맑아야…'.

examples.ko: 모기가 귀 옆에서 윙윙거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: A mosquito buzzed next to my ear, so I couldn't sleep.
Bees are buzzing around the flowers.
The fan whirred all night.

examples.ko: 윙윙거리는 소리 때문에 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: I can't concentrate because of the buzzing sound.
A fly is buzzing around over the food.
I get annoyed every time a mosquito buzzes.

explain: 벌, 모기, 선풍기, 기계처럼 낮고 가늘게 이어지는 소리를 낼 때 써요. 귀에서 윙윙 소리가 나는 느낌을 말할 때도 '귀가 윙윙거려요'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes the low, continuous sound made by bees, mosquitoes, fans and machines. It is also used for ringing in the ears, as in '귀가 윙윙거려요'.

examples.en: A fly keeps buzzing around inside the room.
The strong wind whistled through the wires all night.
The baby woke up to the whirring of the vacuum cleaner.

examples.ko: 작은 벌이 윙윙대며 꽃 위를 날았어요.
examples.en: A small bee flew over the flowers, buzzing.
The machine next door was whirring, so I slept badly.

examples.ko: 드론이 하늘에서 윙윙댈 때 사람들이 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: When the drone buzzed in the sky, people looked up.

explain: '윙윙거리다'와 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 써도 돼요. 벌레, 바람, 기계가 계속 내는 낮은 소리에 쓰고, 시끄럽거나 신경 쓰이는 느낌이 자주 있어요.
explain_en: It means the same as '윙윙거리다', so you can swap them. It is used for the low continuous sound of insects, wind and machines, and it often feels noisy or annoying.

examples.ko: 빨간 코트를 입은 사람이 사람들 사이에서 유난히 눈에 띄었어요.
examples.en: The person in the red coat stood out especially among the crowd.

examples.ko: 오늘따라 보름달이 유난히 크고 밝아서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The full moon was unusually big and bright today, so I took a photo.

examples.ko: 그렇게 유난 떨지 말고 편하게 있어요.
examples.en: Don't make such a fuss; just relax.
That friend is particularly fussy about cleanliness.
The child made such a fuss in the restaurant that it was hard.

examples.ko: 다들 조용한데 너만 왜 이렇게 유난이에요?
examples.en: Everyone else is quiet, so why are you the only one making such a fuss?

explain: 실제로는 부사 '유난히'로 가장 많이 쓰고, 평소나 다른 것과 다르게 두드러진다는 느낌이에요. 명사로는 '유난(을) 떨다'처럼 말하고, 이때는 호들갑스럽다는 약간 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 별일도 아닌데 왜 그렇게 유난을 떨어요?
phrases.nuance_ko: 별것 아닌 일에 지나치게 호들갑스럽게 행동한다는 뜻이에요. 상대를 약간 나무라는 말투로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means acting overly dramatic about something minor. It is often said with a slightly scolding tone.

explain_en: It appears most often as the adverb '유난히', which carries the sense of standing out from the usual or from others. As a noun it is used in '유난(을) 떨다', which has a slightly negative feel of making too much fuss.

examples.ko: 계약 조건은 서명하기 전에 꼭 유념해 두세요.
examples.en: Please be sure to keep the contract terms in mind before signing.

examples.ko: 어린이 보호 구역에서는 속도를 줄여야 한다는 점을 늘 유념하며 운전해요.
examples.en: I always drive keeping in mind that I must slow down in school zones.

examples.ko: 약은 식후에 먹어야 한다는 점을 유념하세요.
examples.en: Please keep in mind that you should take this medicine after meals.
I'll keep that point in mind from now on.

examples.ko: 이번 일을 계기로 안전 수칙에 더 유념했어요.
examples.en: After this incident, I paid more attention to the safety rules.

examples.ko: 유념하지 않으면 같은 실수를 되풀이할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't keep it in mind, you may repeat the same mistake.

explain: '~점을 유념하다', '~에 유념하다'처럼 쓰고, 주의할 것을 마음에 두고 신경 쓴다는 느낌이에요. '명심하다'는 깊이 새긴다는 느낌이 더 강하고, '유념하세요'는 안내문이나 당부하는 말에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is used as '~점을 유념하다' or '~에 유념하다', meaning to keep something to be careful about in mind. '명심하다' feels stronger, as if engraving it deep in your mind, and '유념하세요' is often heard in notices and cautions.

examples.ko: 둘째 날에 유람선을 타고 바다를 구경했어요.
examples.en: On the second day, we took a cruise boat and enjoyed the sea.
The Han River cruise is especially pretty for the night view.
I went on a lake outing over the weekend.

examples.ko: 옛날 선비들은 산천을 유람하며 시를 지었어요.
examples.en: Scholars of old toured mountains and rivers and wrote poems.
The sightseeing course takes about an hour.
After the island tour ended, we returned to the pier.

explain: '여행'이나 '관광'보다 한가롭게 풍경을 즐기며 돌아다닌다는 느낌이에요. 단독보다 '유람선', '유람 코스'처럼 합쳐서 많이 쓰고, 옛날 이야기에서는 '산천을 유람하다'처럼 나와요.
explain_en: Compared with '여행' or '관광', it feels more leisurely, like wandering to enjoy the scenery. It is more often used in compounds such as '유람선' and '유람 코스' than alone, and old stories use it as '산천을 유람하다'.

examples.en: It's the weekend, so a lot of sightseers have gathered.
An announcement was made for the sightseers.
Sightseers have to buy tickets at the pier.

examples.ko: 호수에 유람객 몇 명이 배를 타고 있어요.
examples.en: A few sightseers are riding a boat on the lake.
The boat rocked, so the sightseers were startled.

examples.ko: 유람객의 안전을 위해 구명조끼를 입어야 해요.
examples.en: For the safety of sightseers, you must wear a life jacket.

explain: 일상에서는 '관광객'이 훨씬 일반적이고, '유람객'은 유람선이나 뱃놀이처럼 경치를 즐기는 장면에서 써요. 뉴스나 안내문에서 가끔 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: In daily life '관광객' is far more general, while '유람객' is used in scenes of enjoying scenery, such as a cruise or boat ride. You may occasionally see it in news and notices.

examples.ko: 이번 대회에서는 그가 우승 후보로 유력시돼요.
examples.en: In this tournament, he is seen as the likely favorite to win.

examples.ko: 그 팀의 우승이 유력시된다고 기자가 말했어요.
examples.en: The reporter said that the team's victory looks very likely.

examples.ko: 새 대표로 김 의원이 유력시되고 있어요.
examples.en: Assemblyman Kim is seen as the likely new leader.
A short circuit was seen as the most likely cause of the fire.
The candidate who had been seen as the front-runner suddenly gave up.

examples.ko: 그가 유력시되는 이유는 경험이 많기 때문이에요.
examples.en: The reason he is seen as the front-runner is that he has a lot of experience.

explain: 우승, 당선, 원인처럼 결과나 사실이 그럴 가능성이 가장 크다고 볼 때 써요. 주로 뉴스에서 '~이/가 유력시되다'로 나오고, 비슷한 '유력하다'는 '당선이 유력하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when something such as a win, an election result or a cause is seen as the most likely one. It mostly appears in the news as '~이/가 유력시되다', and the similar '유력하다' is used as in '당선이 유력하다'.

examples.en: An influential person in that area sponsored the event.
I started the business without help from anyone powerful.
The influential people of the village gathered and held a meeting.
There is a rumor that he is close to a powerful figure in politics.
If I ask a powerful person, will things work out quickly?

examples.ko: 유력자라고 해서 법을 어겨도 되는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Being influential doesn't mean you can break the law.

explain: 정치, 경제, 지역 사회에서 영향력이 큰 사람을 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '실력자'가 있고, 연줄이나 힘을 가진 사람이라는 느낌이 있어서 문맥에 따라 약간 부정적으로 들리기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a person with great influence in politics, business or a local community. A similar word is '실력자', and it suggests someone with connections and power, so depending on context it can sound slightly negative.
